turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start with who decided that and when.
Your problem. I'm listening, Hale, and I'm writing it down.
I'm getting dozens of these essays now. What would a fair process for catching AI writing look like? What would you put in the policy?

You're asking me to write your policy for you? Your school already has one, I printed it from the website, and you skipped the part where you call the parent before the mark goes in. Owen's essay is what we're here about, so tell me why that zero is still in the gradebook.
